core_obligations: Derive the bijection between sections and surjections onto invertible modules from the functor of points (proof lines 8219-8224).
Show that any section is a closed immersion (proof lines 8225-8227).
Define the local map f = k/s into the conormal sheaf and prove it is well defined (proof lines 8228-8241 and 8265-8271).
Identify D_+(s) = Spec(Sym(K)) and prove the isomorphism with the conormal sheaf (proof lines 8243-8264).
difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma: for a quasi-coherent module E on a scheme X there is a bijection between sections sigma of the projective bundle P(E) -> X and surjections E -> L onto an invertible module, the section is a closed immersion, and the conormal sheaf of its image is canonically Ker(E -> L) (x) L^{-1}; both the bijection and the isomorphism are compatible with base change (source lines 8189-8217). The proof reads the sections off the functor of points, uses separatedness of the projection to get a closed immersion, and then makes the conormal computation explicit over an affine open, where E -> L corresponds to M -> N with M = K (+) A s, Sym(M) = Sym(K)[s] and D_+(s) = Spec(Sym(K)), proving independence of the chosen generator by the identity k/s' = (k/s)(1 + k'/s)^{-1}.
